source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12 ("Derry local elections: contests threatened in two county council divisions. Nominations received")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: the only candidate left after withdrawals (Belfast News-Letter, 22 and 29 April 1927)

note: Nominations were received on 21 April 1927 and printed in the Belfast News-Letter of 22 April, with retiring members marked by an asterisk; withdrawals closed on 28 April (News-Letter, 29 April). Marcus Smyth and Wm. H. Reed withdrew in Faughanvale, leaving George Leeke returned unopposed, so Bellarena alone was contested, between Wm. Loughrey and J. C. Drennan, both Unionists. The poll was taken on Friday 27 May 1927 and the votes were counted on Saturday morning, 28 May, when Drennan was returned by 505 to 496 (Londonderry Sentinel, 31 May 1927). No nominations were received for Dungiven or Claudy, whose sitting members Patrick M'Closkey and Cyril A. Nicholson were treated as re-elected. Polled Friday 27 May 1927: 'Polling took place yesterday in the Bellarena division of county Londonderry, the only division in the county where there was a contest' (Londonderry Sentinel, Saturday 28 May 1927, p. 8). Re-filed from 1927-05-26 (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026), which had been inferred from the Saturday count. Returned unopposed.
